generation.explanation: A secant line cuts a curve at two points, P at x = a and Q at x = a + h, and its slope is the difference quotient (f(a+h) − f(a))/h. As h shrinks toward 0, Q slides along the curve toward P and the secant line rotates into the tangent line — the line that just kisses the curve at P. The limiting slope is the derivative f′(a) = lim(h→0) [f(a+h) − f(a)]/h. Drag the yellow point anywhere along the parabola, shrink h with the slider (or press the animate button), and watch the orange secant settle onto the green true tangent as their slopes merge.
